title: Settlement Basis: Credit Reissue Fee on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
The reissue fee charged for putting a lapsed travel credit back into use under Air Ticket Fare Brands is the credit reissue fee of the fare brand that produced the voucher, taken once for the voucher.

**What the determination reads.** The fare brand that produced the voucher is the fare brand held on the air booking the voucher was issued on, and its credit reissue fee is the figure published against that brand in the Air Ticket Fare Brands tariff. The travel credit vouchers standing on the booking supply their issue lines, the traveller position each line carries, the value each voucher stands at, the day each was issued and the day each lapses.

**Whether an amount is owed.** The travel credit vouchers standing on the booking are taken as one set, and the set stands lapsed when the voucher most recently issued on it has lapsed. Where that voucher has not lapsed, the set is still redeemable as it stands and nothing is owed under this rule. The voucher most recently issued settles the question for the whole set: where it is still live the set is redeemable although an earlier voucher on the booking has lapsed, and where it has lapsed the set stands lapsed.

**Against which line the fee is raised.** The fee is filed against the issue line of the largest lapsed voucher standing on the booking, and it carries the traveller position of that line. Where the booking carries lapsed vouchers of differing value, it is the largest of them whose issue line and traveller position are taken.

**The two stages in which the fee is settled.** The fee is settled in two stages, and each stage has its own name. The tariff component is settled first: it is the credit reissue fee of the fare brand that produced the voucher, taken at whatever loading the time the credit has stood unclaimed earns and then taken as many times as the fee falls due on the booking. The fee charged is that tariff component with anything added to it in dollars, added once for the booking and never once for each voucher, and with any relief then taken as a share of the whole, each share and each uplift that bears on a figure acting in turn on the figure the one before it gives, so that the figure runs on from one step to the next and is never reached by measuring them separately against the tariff component as it was settled and netting the results together.

**How several adjustments on one figure meet.** Where more than one share is taken on the same figure, the shares act one after another, each on the figure the one before it gives, and are never combined into a single rate; where more than one uplift is added to the same figure, the uplifts are combined into a single uplift and the figure is increased once by that total.

**Rounding.** The fee charged is rounded to two decimal places at the end and never at any intermediate step.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** All the figures below are hypothetical, chosen only to show how the two stages meet, and none of them is a published rate. Suppose the credit reissue fee of the fare brand that produced the voucher stands at 40.00 US dollars, suppose the voucher most recently issued on the booking has lapsed, so that the set stands lapsed, suppose the time the credit has stood unclaimed earns a loading of one and one tenth, and suppose the fee falls due twice on the booking. Settling the first stage: 40.00 US dollars taken at a loading of one and one tenth is 44.00 US dollars, and taken twice is 88.00 US dollars, so the tariff component stands at 88.00 US dollars. The fee charged follows from that settled figure, step by step. Suppose a share of 0.62 bears on it: 88.00 taken at 0.62 gives 54.56. Suppose an uplift of 0.33 then bears on the figure that share gave: 54.56 increased by 0.33 gives 72.5648. Suppose 15.00 US dollars then falls to be added in dollars, which is added once for the booking and not once for each of the two takings, so it lands on the figure the uplift gave, giving 87.5648. Suppose relief of one quarter is then taken as a share of the whole as it then stands, which is 21.8912 US dollars, leaving 65.6736 US dollars. Each step is worked on the figure the step before it gave, and no step is worked on the 88.00 the first stage settled at; nothing is rounded along the way. Rounded to two decimal places at the end, the fee charged is 65.67 US dollars. Had the voucher most recently issued on that booking still been live, the set would be redeemable as it stands and nothing would be owed.
